oodles.e: Uncertain; perhaps from scadoodles (“unspecified large amount, number, or quantity”) (US, slang) (although the Oxford English Dictionary notes this is attested slightly later), or from boodle (“whole collection or lot”) (US, dialectal), caboodle (“large collection of people or things”) (US, slang) + -s (suffix forming pluralia tantum).

s.d: a large number or amount
x: made lots of new friends
she amassed stacks of newspapers

s.d: (informal) unspecified large amount, number, or quantity; lots, tons.
x: Minimalist yet soothing décor, private pools and steam rooms […] and simply oodles of class make this one of the island's top choices. Honeymoon, anyone?

An exclamation of ooh.
x: In any given performance, their tosses and spins and leaps elicit oohs and ahhs from children and adults.

The most underrated component in building a custom gun is the metalsmithing. Stock work immediately attracts attention. Fancy checkering patterns, meticulously executed, are sure to elicit oohs and ahhs.

x: They oohed and aahed when they unwrapped the presents

s.d: To exclaim ooh.
x: When they went into the royal chambers, we could hear them oohing and aahing.
In the next few minutes, Molly tossed dress after dress aside, oohing and aahing at the varied fabrics, the elaborate detailing of each one, until she found a dress that was— / Breathtaking.

s.d: An expression of surprise.

x: Ooh, I love that book!

oology.e: From oo- (“relating to eggs or ova”, prefix) + -logy (“branch of learning or study of a subject”, suffix). The word is cognate with French oologie, Late Latin ōologia.

s.d: the branch of zoology that studies eggs (especially birds' eggs and their size, shape, coloration, and number)
(uncountable) The study of birds' eggs.
(uncountable) The hobby or practice of collecting birds' eggs, especially those of wild birds.
x: Barely a day went by when Franklin [Delano Roosevelt] didn't talk about the world of birds. At ten years old he started dabbling in oology, the collecting of eggs and nests.

oolong.e: 1850s. From either Mandarin 烏龍 /乌龙 (wūlóng) due to hypercorrection, or directly from Hokkien 烏龍 /乌龙 (o͘-liông), from 烏 /乌 (o͘, “black”) + 龍 /龙 (liông, “dragon”). See also pouchong from Hokkien 包種茶 /包种茶 (pau-chióng-tê, literally “tea of the wrapped kind”).

s.d: Chinese tea leaves that have been partially fermented before being dried
(uncountable) A partially fermented tea, often roasted, which combines the characteristics of green tea and black tea.
x: Near-synonym: black dragon

Flavour and aroma of semi-fermented teas is dictated by the extent of fermentation and, for this reason, oolong has a considerably stronger flavour than pouchong, which undergoes a significantly shorter fermentation.

s.d: attractiveness to the opposite sex
the activeness of an energetic personality
(informal, uncountable) Strength, power, passion or effectiveness; clout.
x: Use a mild cleanser, but pick something with enough oomph to do the job.
"Yes, well they're finding it difficult, sir. They are afflicted with a certain lassitude. They're just finding it hard to get behind the job. They lack oomph."

s.d: (informal, uncountable) Sex appeal.
x: 'Come to think of it, the girl looked a bit like Ann,' Jerry reflected. 'Foxy, know what I mean? Garbo eyes, lots of oomph.'

s.d: A bassy grunting or thudding sound.
To produce a bassy grunting or thudding sound.
surgical removal of one or both ovaries
(uncountable) The surgical removal of one or both ovaries, usually performed to treat or prevent conditions such as ovarian cancer, ovarian cysts, endometriosis, or other ovarian disorders.
inflammation of one or both ovaries
surgical removal of one or both ovaries and the corresponding Fallopian tubes

oosphere.e:
PIE word
 *h₂ōwyóm
From oo- (prefix denoting something relating to eggs or ova) + -sphere, modelled after French oosphère.

s.d: a gamete; used especially of lower plants
A large nonmotile egg cell, especially of an alga or fungus, formed in an oogonium and ready for fertilization.
a thick-walled sexual spore that develops from a fertilized oosphere in some algae and fungi
mature ovum after penetration by sperm but before the formation of a zygote
The haploid cell, produced by meiotic division of a secondary oocyte, that is a nearly mature ovum.
x: Beyond the last of the oocytes, toward the lumen, are found numerous closely packed ootids, which have small pronuclei and are less basophilic than the smaller oocytes, due to the accumulated yolk in the cytoplasm.

This process, which now requires 45 min instead of the 20 min needed after hormone stimulation or MPF transfer does not correspond to the amplification of an eventual residual MPF present in the ootid.

ooze.e:
* (Noun) Middle English wose (“sap”), from Old English wōs (“sap, froth”), from Proto-Germanic *wōsą, from Proto-Indo-European *wóseh₂ (“sap”) (cf. Sanskrit वसा (vásā, “fat”)). Cognate to Middle Low German wose (“scum”), Old High German wasal (“rain”), Old Swedish os, oos, ooss, Swedish os. Compare Old Swedish os, oos, Swedish os, Danish os, Norwegian os (“fumes, vapors, reeking, fug”).
* (Verb) Middle English wosen, from Old English wōsan; see above. Compare Swedish osa (“ooze”).

s.d: any thick, viscous matter
the process of seeping
(uncountable) Tanning liquor, an aqueous extract of vegetable matter (tanbark, sumac, etc.) in a tanning vat used to tan leather.
(uncountable) An oozing, gentle flowing, or seepage, as of water through sand or earth.
(obsolete, uncountable) Secretion, humour.
(obsolete, uncountable) Juice, sap.
(uncountable) Soft mud, slime, or shells especially in the bed of a river or estuary.
x: my son i' th' ooze is bedded.

s.d: (uncountable) A pelagic marine sediment containing a significant amount of the microscopic remains of either calcareous or siliceous planktonic debris organisms.
x: Seaweed were left on the blackened marble, while the salt ooze defaced the matchless works of art.

s.d: (uncountable) A piece of soft, wet, pliable ground.
pass gradually or leak through or as if through small openings
release (a liquid) in drops or small quantities
x: exude sweat through the pores

s.d: (figuratively) To be secreted or slowly leak.
x: I promised him I would keep silence, but the story gradually oozed out, and the Cronsons left the country.
Pale slime oozed through all the surfaces; some of it dripped from the ceiling and burned Dennis as badly as the blazing sparks had done a moment before.

s.d: (figuratively) To give off a strong sense of (something); to exude.
x: […] this room, where misfortune seems to ooze, where speculation lurks in corners, and of which Madame Vauquer inhales the warm, fetid air without being nauseated.
"Good servants are so hard to find," Chesna said, oozing arrogance.

s.d: a very soft leather made from the skins of calves and having a suede finish on the flesh side

(uncountable) Leather made from sheep and calf skins by mechanically forcing ooze through their pores; especially, such leather with a soft, finely granulated suede-like finish (sometimes called velvet finish) applied to the flesh side for special purposes. Ooze leather is used for shoe uppers, in bookbinding, making wallets or handbags, mostly.
release (a liquid) in drops or small quantities
x: exude sweat through the pores

s.d: run slowly and gradually
x: Blood oozed through the bandage

s.d: the process of seeping
(uncountable) Something that oozes; a seepage.
x: A 12-acre field of good, deep land on the farm of Frenchlaw, in Berwickshire, was rendered swampy by springs and oozings of water from the surrounding rising ground being retained upon the clay subsoil.

s.d: (uncountable) Synonym of stringing (“defect in 3D printing”).
x: One of the side effects of having the hot end set to the optimal temperature for extrusion is oozing.

s.d: leaking out slowly

s.d: leaking out slowly
Of or pertaining to the quality of something that oozes.
x:
A daughter?
Oh heauens, that they were liuing both in Nalpes
The King and Queene there, that they were, I wish
My selfe were mudded in that oo-zie bed
Where my sonne lies: when did you lose your daughter?
[The rain] fell with an oozy, slushy sound among the grass; and made a muddy kennel of every furrow in the ploughed fields.
